name: Specific Antibody Deficiency with Normal Immunoglobulin Concentrations and Normal Numbers of B Cells

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Specific Antibody Deficiency

criteria.description: Normal serum concentrations of total immunoglobulins (IgG, IgA, IgM)
Normal peripheral blood B cell numbers by flow cytometry
Poor or absent specific antibody response to polysaccharide vaccines despite normal total immunoglobulins
Exclusion of other primary or secondary immunodeficiencies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of normal total immunoglobulins and normal B cell counts with impaired specific antibody response to polysaccharide vaccines, and exclusion of other immunodeficiencies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires functional antibody testing, typically post-immunization with pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine.

pathognomonic.notes: Includes frequent otitis media, sinusitis, and pneumonia

pathognomonic.symptomName: Poor antibody response to polysaccharide vaccines
pathognomonic.notes: Demonstrated by inadequate serotype-specific antibody titers post-vaccination
searchTerms: poor vaccine response to polysaccharide types
weak antibody production after certain vaccines

common.notes: Persistent or repeated inflammation of the paranasal sinuses
Lower respiratory tract infections with bacterial etiology

common.symptomName: Increased susceptibility to encapsulated bacterial infections
common.notes: Notably Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae
searchTerms: increased risk of infections from encapsulated bacteria
higher susceptibility to coated bacterial infections

occasional.notes: Persistent cough related to recurrent infections
Structural lung damage secondary to recurrent infections
Generalized tiredness due to ongoing illness

rare.notes: Rarely associated with autoimmune cytopenias or other autoimmune disorders
Severe systemic infection is uncommon but possible

laboratory: Normal serum IgG, IgA, and IgM concentrations
Normal peripheral blood B cell counts by flow cytometry
Impaired specific antibody response to polysaccharide vaccines (e.g., pneumococcal vaccine)
Normal T cell numbers and function
imaging: Chest radiographs or CT showing bronchiectasis in some cases
Sinus imaging may show chronic sinusitis
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; heterogeneous etiology
other: Poor vaccine responsiveness despite normal immunoglobulin levels

distinguishingFeatures: Reduced B cell numbers or function
Broader immune defects including T cell abnormalities
Normal total IgG but deficiency in one or more IgG subclasses
May have normal or reduced B cell numbers
Transient low immunoglobulin levels in infants

redFlags: Recurrent severe bacterial infections requiring hospitalization
Poor or absent antibody response to polysaccharide vaccines
Development of bronchiectasis or chronic lung disease
references: Orange JS, Ballow M, Stiehm ER, et al. Use and interpretation of diagnostic vaccination in primary immunodeficiency: a working group report of the Basic and Clinical Immunology Interest Section of the American Academy of Allergy, Asthma & Immunology.
